paragraphs: EverestLabs sells vision AI, software agents and robotics meant to digitize and automate material processing plants. The company frames the work as transforming recycled and virgin material processing. Its stated buyers are operators in recycling, resource recovery, metals, e-waste, packaging, and mining.

The software side, Navigator, is described as a vision and agentic AI platform that gives every operator a process engineer, an equipment expert, and a data analyst in one chat. EverestLabs states that Navigator never acts autonomously. Equipment presets are applied only once an operator approves them. On the hardware side, the robotic sorting cell has a compact 3x3 ft footprint and works over existing conveyor belts without expensive retrofit. Those cells are presented as fully turnkey and remotely managed, delivered by a 24/7 staffed Remote Operations Center.

The company says its vision system covers 65 or more material classes at over 95% detection accuracy. On commercial terms, the site says payback lands in under 12 months, guaranteed by SLA. EverestLabs is headquartered in Fremont, California.
